newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Umax-M'bishi unit to invest T$38b in chip plant.
newsitem.headline: Umax-M'bishi unit to invest T$38b in chip plant.

text.p: Taiwan's Powerchip Co, a joint venture of Umax-Elite group and Mitsubishi Electric, said on Wednesday it planned to invest a further T$38 billion into its planned second memory-chip plant.
The firm said in a statement the extra funding would enable it to equip the new plant to make advanced 12-inch dynamic random-access memory wafers as well as eight-inch DRAM wafers.
"Producing 12-inch wafers should be the future trend, and all major firms in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan are all speeding up their development," the statement said.
The T$38 billion brings Powerchip's investments in new wafer projects to T$50 billion.
Powerchip said it had applied to the government for listing in Taiwan's fledgling but rapidly growing over-the-counter stock exchange in order to raise funds for chip projects.
"We expect the Securities and Futures Commission to grant us listing permission in January 1998 and we will be listed officially in March," Powerchip chairman Huang Chung-jen said.
Its expansion plans called for building a second plant and upgrading the first plant's monthly capacity to 25,000 DRAMs.

Powerchip is one of several Taiwan chipmakers enlisting technological assistance from Japanese allies to compete against Korean giants like Samsung Electronics in the global market for advanced DRAMs.
Powerchip said construction of the plant would begin at the end of 1997 and production of 12-inch wafers would commence in 2000 at a monthly capacity of 20,000 pieces.
The bulk of production would focus on advanced 64-megabit dynamic random access memory chips, Powerchip said.
"We also do not rule out making 256-megabit DRAMs if market development calls for it," the company said.
Powerchip currently has one wafer plant in Taiwan that produces 15,000 DRAMs per month.
